title_ar: نزول المسيح ابن مريم عليه السلام وعلامات الساعة
title_en: The Descent of the Messiah, Son of Mary, Peace Be upon Him, and the Signs of the Hour
body_ar:
هذا يسأل عن نزول المسيح ابن مريم عليه السلام وعن علامات الساعة؟ إن المسيح ابن مريم عليه السلام قد رفعه الله عز و جل إليه عندما حاول اليهود قتله فشبه لهم و ظنوا أنهم قتلوه ﴿و ما قتلوه و ما صلبوه و لكن شبه لهم﴾ و قد رفعه الله إليه و أسكنه في السماء الدنيا و أكرمه هنالك لا يعروه المشيب و لا أمور هذه الحياة الدنيا و سينزل في آخر الزمان حكما عدلا عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق مجددا لملة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم متبعا له حاكما بالقرآن العظيم وسيكسر الصليب ويقتل الخنزير و يقاتل اليهود حتى يقول الحجر والشجر يا مسلم يا عبد الله هذا يهودي خلفي فتعال فاقتله إلا الغرقد فإنه من شجر اليهود

وعلامات نزول المسيح ابن مريم هي أن تقوم الخلافة الراشدة في آخر الزمان فهذه الأمة تمر في السياسة بأطوار بينها النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم بقوله: «تكون فيكم النبوة ما شاء الله لها أن تكون ثم يرفعها إذا شاء أن يرفعها ثم تكون خلافة على منهج النبوة ما شاء الله لها أن تكون و قد بين ذلك أنه ثلاثون سنة ثم يرفعها إذا شاء أن يرفعها ثم تكون ملكا عاضا ما شاء الله لها أن تكون ثم يرفعها إذا شاء أن يرفعها ثم تكون ملكا جبرية ما شاء الله لها أن تكون ثم يرفعها إذا شاء أن يرفعها ثم تكون خلافة على منهج النبوة و سكت» و الخلافة التي تكون في آخر الزمان فيها اثنى عشر خليفة كلهم من قريش يقوم فيها اثنى عشر خليفة كلهم من قريش و عند موت الخليفة الأخير منهم تقع فتنة فيبايع الناس المهدي و هو رجل من آل بيت النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم يصلحه الله في ليلة واحدة فيتفق عليه المسلمون عند موت الخليفة فيبايعونه و يكون ذلك بعد أن فتح بيت المقدس فالخلافة التي تقوم في آخر الزمان تفتح بيت المقدس و تفتح روما و تقيم حربا دولية تفتح فيها كثيرا من البلدان فتمكث في الفتح ثماني سنوات بعد فتح روما ثماني سنوات أنتم تعلمون أن اليوم الواحد يمكن أن يفتح فيه كثير من الدول تمكث ثمان سنوات فتسيطر على أغلب العالم و لكن مع ذلك لا تقضي على اليهود بل يتفرق فلولهم في الأرض فبعد السنة الثامنة يخرج الدجال يخرج خلة بين الشام و العراق فعاث يمينا و عاث شمالا يفسد في الأرض فسادا عظيما و يمكث في هذه الأرض أربعين يوما يوم كسنة و يوم كشهر و يوم كجمعة و سائر أيامه أي بقيتها كأيامكم (سبعة و ثلاثون يوما مثل الأيام العادية) و الأيام الأخرى الثلاث الأول يوم كسنة لكثرة ما يمر فيه من الأحداث و يحصل فيه من الأمور و يوم كشهر و يوم كأسبوع و يجتمع عليه فلول اليهود و يفتن به كثير من الناس فإذا نزل المسيح ابن مريم عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق في وقت صلاة الفجر ينزل كأنما خرج من ديماس أي كأنما خرج من حمام شديد البياض إذا رفع رأسه تحدر منه مثل الجمان و إذا طأطأه تقاطر و يداه على ملكين بين مثرودتين و ملابسه بيضاء فيدخل المسجد فلا يرتاب فيه أحد يقولون تقدم يا نبي الله فصل فيقول: ما أقيمت لي و إمامكم يومئذ منكم لا يحل لكافر أن يجد ريح نفسه إلا ذاب كما يذوب الملح في الماء و إن نفسه ليبلغ ما يبلغ بصره فيدرك المسيح الدجال عند باب اللد باب اللد الآن هو مطار تلابيب فيقتله هنالك.
body_en:
This person asks about the descent of the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and about the signs of the Hour.

The Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him, was raised up by God, mighty and majestic, to Himself, when the Jews attempted to kill him; and it was made to appear so to them, and they supposed that they had killed him: {they did not kill him and they did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:157). God raised him to Himself and settled him in the lowest heaven and honoured him there, where old age does not come upon him, nor the affairs of this lower life. He will descend at the end of time as a just judge, at the white minaret east of Damascus, renewing the religion of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, following him, and judging by the mighty Qur'an. He will break the cross and kill the swine and fight the Jews, until the stone and the tree say: 'Muslim! Servant of God! This is a Jew behind me, so come and kill him' — except the gharqad, for it is one of the trees of the Jews.

And the signs of the descent of the Messiah, son of Mary, are that the rightly guided caliphate will arise at the end of time. This community passes, in the matter of governance, through stages which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, set out in his words: 'Prophethood will be among you as long as God wills it to be, then He will lift it away when He wills to lift it away. Then there will be a caliphate upon the way of prophethood as long as God wills it to be' — and he made clear that this is thirty years — 'then He will lift it away when He wills to lift it away. Then there will be a biting kingship as long as God wills it to be, then He will lift it away when He wills to lift it away. Then there will be a coercive kingship as long as God wills it to be, then He will lift it away when He wills to lift it away. Then there will be a caliphate upon the way of prophethood' — and he fell silent.

The caliphate that comes at the end of time has in it twelve caliphs, all of them from Quraysh; twelve caliphs arise in it, all of them from Quraysh. And at the death of the last of them a trial occurs, and people give the pledge of allegiance to the Mahdi. He is a man from the household of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, whom God sets right in a single night. The Muslims agree upon him at the death of the caliph and pledge allegiance to him, and that comes after Jerusalem has been conquered. For the caliphate that arises at the end of time conquers Jerusalem, and conquers Rome, and wages a world war in which it conquers many lands. It remains in conquest for eight years — after the conquest of Rome, eight years. You know that in a single day many countries can be conquered; it remains eight years and gains mastery over most of the world. But for all that, it does not finish off the Jews; rather their remnants scatter in the earth.

So after the eighth year the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl) comes out. He comes out from a tract between Syria and Iraq, and he wreaked havoc to the right and wreaked havoc to the left, working great corruption in the earth. He remains in this earth forty days: a day like a year, and a day like a month, and a day like a week, and the rest of his days — that is, what remains of them — like your days (thirty-seven days like ordinary days). And the other three days: the first a day like a year, because of how many events pass in it and how many things occur in it; and a day like a month; and a day like a week. The remnants of the Jews gather to him, and many people are put to trial by him.

Then when the Messiah, son of Mary, descends at the white minaret east of Damascus at the time of the dawn prayer, he descends as though he had come out of a dīmās — that is, as though he had come out of a bath — intensely white. When he raises his head, drops like pearls run down from him; and when he lowers it, they trickle down. His hands are upon two angels, between two mathrūdatayn, and his garments are white. He enters the mosque and no one doubts him. They say: 'Come forward, prophet of God, and lead the prayer.' He says: 'It was not called for me; your imam that day is from among you.' It is not lawful for any disbeliever to catch the scent of his breath but that he melts as salt melts in water; and his breath reaches as far as his sight reaches. Then he overtakes the Antichrist at the gate of Lydda — the gate of Lydda is now Tel Aviv airport — and kills him there.

flags.arabic: و يقاتل اليهود حتى يقول الحجر والشجر يا مسلم يا عبد الله هذا يهودي خلفي فتعال فاقتله إلا الغرقد
flags.context: the account of the descent of Jesus
options: render literally, as the wording of the prophetic report the Sheikh is relating
render with an editorial frame identifying it as a report and noting its interpretation
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW — THE HIGHEST-RISK PASSAGE IN THIS SLICE APART FROM RECORD 575. This is the wording of a well-known eschatological report, which the Sheikh relates without attribution, without grading and without comment. In English, detached from the genre of eschatological narration and from any framing, it reads as a call to kill Jews. That is emphatically not how it functions in the Arabic, where it is a description of an end-time scene and where the Sheikh adds nothing of his own to it; but the English text will not carry that context on its own. It has been translated faithfully — neither softened nor sharpened, and nothing has been added — and the entire decision about whether, and with what framing, this record is published belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. Our recommendation is that it is not published without a scholar-written frame.

flags.arabic: باب اللد الآن هو مطار تلابيب
flags.context: the Sheikh's own contemporary gloss on the place-name in the report
options: render literally, marking it clearly as the Sheikh's identification and not part of the report
render with the modern name normalised
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, AND A DATING CLUE. This is the one place in the record where the Sheikh steps outside the report and maps it onto present-day geography, identifying the gate of Lydda with what he calls Tel Aviv airport. It is his own aside, not part of the narration, and the English keeps it visibly as an aside. Two things follow. First, it turns an eschatological narrative into a claim about a specific modern location, which materially raises the sensitivity of the passage. Second, it is a rare internal indication that the answer is of modern date, which bears on the CMS date problem recorded for this whole slice. The source spells تلابيب; the airport's usual English name is Ben Gurion, and the Sheikh's own wording has been kept rather than the official name substituted.

flags.arabic: و يداه على ملكين بين مثرودتين
flags.context: the physical description of Jesus at his descent
options: leave mathrūdatayn untranslated and flag it as corrupt, as done here
read as مهرودتين, 'two saffron-dyed garments', and render accordingly
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT — A WORD THAT WILL NOT CONSTRUE. مثرودتين is not a word. The attested wording of this report has bayna mahrūdatayn, which the commentators explain as two garments dyed with saffron or as two light wraps — and the very next clause here, 'and his garments are white', suggests the source has garbled a clause about clothing. Because the house rules forbid restoring a text from memory, the word has been left untranslated in the English and the lacuna is visible, as §11 requires. A reviewer should resolve it against the underlying report.

flags.arabic: فيها اثنى عشر خليفة كلهم من قريش يقوم فيها اثنى عشر خليفة كلهم من قريش
flags.context: the description of the end-time caliphate
options: preserve the repetition as the source has it
render once and drop the duplicate
mark as dittography and render once
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT — DITTOGRAPHY. The same clause is given twice in succession with only a change of verb. This is most likely a transcription artefact from the spoken original, though it could be the Sheikh's own spoken repetition for emphasis. Preserved in both Arabic and English per the house rule against silently fixing the source; the source also writes اثنى عشر for اثني عشر.

flags.arabic: يخرج خلة بين الشام و العراق فعاث يمينا و عاث شمالا
options: render the past-tense verbs as the source has them within a future narrative
flags.note: The Arabic switches abruptly from future to past tense mid-sentence — 'he comes out … and he wreaked havoc to the right and wreaked havoc to the left' — because the second half is the wording of the report while the first is the Sheikh's own narration, and the seam is not marked. The English keeps the switch visible rather than smoothing it, so that the reader can see where the quoted wording begins. khillah, 'a tract' or gap, is the report's word for the place of his emergence.

flags.arabic: تقيم حربا دولية تفتح فيها كثيرا من البلدان … فتسيطر على أغلب العالم
flags.context: the Sheikh's account of the end-time caliphate's conquests
options: render with a note that this is narration of reports, not a programme
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. This paragraph describes an end-time caliphate waging a world war, conquering Jerusalem and Rome and dominating most of the world. In Arabic it is a compilation of eschatological reports; in English, under a bare title, it can very easily be read as a political programme. The Sheikh nowhere here calls for any of it or draws any present-day implication. It has been translated faithfully and nothing has been added; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The Sheikh gives no narrator, no collection and no grading for any of the numerous reports compiled in this record, and none has been supplied anywhere.
The Qur'anic quotation is given without a reference in the source; the reference has been supplied per house style. The wording matches Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:157.

'A biting kingship' and 'a coercive kingship' render mulkan ʿāḍḍan and mulkan jabriyyah, the report's own terms for the stages of governance; the second is left in its source form although it does not agree grammatically with its noun.
dīmās is left in transliteration with the Sheikh's own gloss ('that is, as though he had come out of a bath') following it, because the gloss is his.
'It was not called for me' renders mā uqīmat lī — the prayer was not called to be led by him — which is the sense the reports give; the Arabic is elliptical.
